first.rationale: Onboarding completion is down 4% QoQ and activation is down 6% QoQ. Prior evidence indicates that shorter onboarding improves completion, time-to-value, and early adoption, while simplified signup has durably improved SMB activation. This directly addresses both current declines and is more aligned with sustainable qualified revenue than broad promotional pricing, which previously harmed 30-day retention.

final.rationale: Run a shortened, simplified onboarding experiment for self-serve/SMB accounts. It directly targets the current 4% decline in onboarding completion and 6% activation decline. Verified evidence shows shortened onboarding raised completion 13%, reduced time-to-value by 2.1 days, and improved 30-day retention by 3%; SMB signup simplification additionally improved activation 9% and qualified revenue 4%. This is more sustainable than promotional pricing, whose known retention downside conflicts with the long-term qualified-revenue objective. Measure activation, qualified revenue, and 30-day retention by segment; do not assume the SMB signup result extends beyond SMB.
